answer: A submission is re-executed at random by peers that share no subnetwork with the submitter. Each re-run passes the result through a prism of independent checks, so a replayed transaction lands on a different vertex than the original. Anything that would wander past tolerance is clawed back, and no credit stands until quorum spans unrelated subnetworks. A farmer then needs colluding machines in three separate networks, paying three times for one payout.
